construct: Carbonic anhydrase II generates intracellular hydrogen ions required for acidification of the osteoclast resorption lacuna. CA2 deficiency impairs osteoclast-mediated mineral dissolution and can also impair renal acidification, producing osteopetrosis with renal tubular acidosis and intracranial calcification.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Dense but fragile bone plus RTA and intracranial calcification with biallelic CA2 variants identifies carbonic-anhydrase-II deficiency; osteoclasts cannot generate enough proton equivalents to acidify the resorption lacuna.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: RANKL differentiation, cathepsin K matrix degradation, integrin attachment, and osteoprotegerin signaling are all real bone-remodeling mechanisms. The CA2 variant plus RTA specifically targets proton generation for lacunar acidification.
